mainTopic: How the סמיכה dispute was settled, אביי's lesson on answering insults, the debate over offerings on יום טוב, and whether blood is sprinkled after a forbidden slaughter of נדרים ונדבות.
overview: The עמוד opens at the end of a story. A man brought many fine animals into the עזרה and invited everyone to do סמיכה on יום טוב, and from that day the הלכה followed בית הלל. In a second story, a student of בית שמאי objects and gets a reply of exactly the same length. From this אביי learns never to answer a sharp remark with more than what was said. A ברייתא then records the back-and-forth between the two schools: בית הלל argue with a קל וחומר and with the פסוק 'לה׳', and בית שמאי answer with נדרים ונדבות and the word 'לכם'. אבא שאול tells בית הלל's argument differently, and the גמרא explains that the two versions disagree about whether נדרים ונדבות may be brought on יום טוב. רב הונא says that on the strict view this ban comes from the Torah, and he proves it from the שתי הלחם. Next, רבא and רבה בר רב הונא discuss someone who slaughtered such an offering on יום טוב anyway, and the גמרא shows when their reasons lead to different rulings. The עמוד ends partway through a ברייתא about the lambs of שבועות that challenges רבה בר רב הונא, and the challenge continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The sheep of Kedar and the day בית הלל won
steps.stepSummary: The story ends: all the fine sheep in ירושלים were brought to the עזרה for public סמיכה, and the הלכה was fixed like בית הלל with no one objecting.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brought all the fine Kedar sheep in ירושלים, stood them in the Temple courtyard, and announced: whoever wants to lean his hands on an animal, come and do it. That day בית הלל won, the הלכה was set like them, and no one there disputed it at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a story that began on the previous עמוד. It tells us how the argument over doing סמיכה on יום טוב was settled in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the story, people were about to follow בית שמאי, who forbid סמיכה on a יום טוב offering. This man made a very public showing of the practice of בית הלל. Because so many people took part in public, the הלכה became fixed like בית הלל, and nobody argued.

keyTerms.meaning: Sheep of Kedar, famous for being top-quality animals
The courtyard of the בית המקדש
Leaning one's hands with force on the head of an offering before it is slaughtered
Their hand prevailed, meaning they won the argument
Disputed or objected

steps.whatToRemember: From this day on, the הלכה about סמיכה on יום טוב follows בית הלל.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה was fixed like בית הלל: סמיכה is done on a יום טוב offering.

steps.title: Two students and two short questions
steps.stepSummary: A student from בית הלל does סמיכה. A student from בית שמאי challenges him, gets an equally short reply, and leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another time, a student of בית הלל brought his עולה to the courtyard to lean on it. A student of בית שמאי met him and said, "What is this leaning?" He answered, "What is this silence?" He silenced him with this rebuke, and the other student walked away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second, short story about the same argument. It shows a student of בית שמאי still objecting after the הלכה was already decided.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The student of בית שמאי asks why the other student is doing סמיכה against בית שמאי's view. The student of בית הלל answers in the same few words: why aren't you keeping quiet, since the הלכה is not like you? The reply works, and the challenger leaves without saying more.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
Silence
A rebuke

phrases.english: Another incident with a certain student
from the students of Beit Hillel
who brought his burnt offering to the courtyard
to lean his hands on it
A certain student found him
from the students of Beit Shammai
He said to him: What is this leaning?
He said to him: What is this silence?
phrases.notes: He means: why aren't you staying quiet? The הלכה wasn't decided your way.

phrases.english: He silenced him with a rebuke
and he went away

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוּב מַעֲשֶׂה בְּתַלְמִיד אֶחָד מִתַּלְמִידֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up story that comes after the הלכה was fixed in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A student of בית הלל defended doing סמיכה on יום טוב with a short reply that matched the challenge.

steps.title: אביי: don't answer back with more than was said
steps.stepSummary: אביי learns from the story that a תלמיד חכם who is challenged should answer with no more words than his friend used.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: So a young Torah scholar whose friend says something sharp to him should not answer back with more than his friend said. In the story, one said "What is this leaning?" and the other answered only "What is this silence?"
steps.whatsHappening: אביי takes a lesson about good behavior from the story just told.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The student of בית הלל was right, but he still matched his reply exactly to the challenge: three words for three words. אביי teaches that when someone speaks sharply to you, you should not escalate. Answer with no more than what was said to you.

keyTerms.meaning: A young Torah scholar
Therefore
To answer back
More

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a lasting rule of דרך ארץ for how Torah scholars should handle sharp words from each other.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Therefore
this young Torah scholar
whose friend says something to him
should not answer him back with words
more than what his friend said to him
for he said to him: "What is this leaning?"
and he answered him back: "What is this silence?"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הִלְכָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a behavior lesson from the story in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not answer a sharp remark with more words than the other person used.

steps.title: בית הלל's קל וחומר for offerings on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: בית הלל argue that if offerings are allowed on שבת, when cooking for people is forbidden, then surely they are allowed on יום טוב, when cooking for people is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: בית הלל said to בית שמאי: If in a place where slaughtering for an ordinary person is forbidden, it is still permitted for the Most High, then in a place where it is permitted for an ordinary person, isn't it logical that it is permitted for the Most High?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with בית הלל's logical proof that עולות may be offered on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת you may not slaughter for your own meal, yet the קרבנות of the מקדש are still offered. On יום טוב you may slaughter for your own meal. So by קל וחומר, offerings for the Most High should surely be allowed on יום טוב too, including the עולות that the two schools argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
An ordinary person, meaning preparing food for people
The Most High, meaning קרבנות offered to ה׳
Isn't it logical? The opening words of a קל וחומר

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי
phrases.english: It was taught: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai
If in a place where it is forbidden for an ordinary person
phrases.notes: "A place" here means a time. This one is שבת.

phrases.english: it is permitted for the Most High
then a place where it is permitted for an ordinary person
isn't it logical that it is permitted for the Most High?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאָסוּר לַהֶדְיוֹט מוּתָּר לַגָּבוֹהַּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new ברייתא about the reasoning behind the dispute.
steps.raayaObject: That עולות may be offered on יום טוב
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from שבת, when קרבנות are offered even though cooking for people is forbidden

steps.title: בית שמאי's counter-example: נדרים ונדבות
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי answer that נדרים ונדבות break the קל וחומר: on יום טוב slaughtering is permitted for people but forbidden for these offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: נדרים ונדבות prove otherwise. On יום טוב, slaughtering is permitted for an ordinary person but forbidden for the Most High.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי reject בית הלל's קל וחומר by pointing to a case where it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל's argument assumed that "allowed for people" means "surely allowed for ה׳." But in this ברייתא both sides accept that נדרים ונדבות are not offered on יום טוב, even though you may slaughter for your own meal that day. So the logic breaks down.

keyTerms.meaning: Vow offerings and gift offerings, which a person takes on voluntarily
Will prove, used to bring a counter-example

steps.confusionAlert: בית שמאי are not saying בית הלל's facts are wrong. They are saying the קל וחומר proves nothing, because one case shows the pattern does not always hold.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to them
Vow offerings and gift offerings will prove
that it is permitted for an ordinary person
and forbidden for the Most High!

steps.triggerLanguage: נְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת יוֹכִיחוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole קל וחומר of בית הלל
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is a known case, נדרים ונדבות, that is permitted for people on יום טוב but forbidden for the Most High.

steps.title: בית הלל: the burnt-offering of appearance has a fixed time
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל reject בית שמאי's comparison. נדרים ונדבות have no fixed time, but a עולת ראיה is tied to the holiday.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to them: You can't learn from vow and gift offerings, because they have no fixed time. Would you say the same about the burnt-offering of appearance, which does have a fixed time?
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל answer בית שמאי's attack from the last step. They show that נדרים ונדבות are not a fair comparison to a עולת ראיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי said that נדרים ונדבות are forbidden on יום טוב, so the קל וחומר falls apart. בית הלל reply that this makes sense for those offerings, since they can be brought any day of the year. A עולת ראיה belongs to the holiday itself, so it should be allowed on the holiday.

keyTerms.meaning: The burnt-offering a person brings when he comes to the בית המקדש on a רגל
It has a fixed, set time
'What about...?' A formula for pointing out a difference that breaks a comparison

phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to them:
What about vow-offerings and gift-offerings?
phrases.notes: He means: why are those forbidden on יום טוב? Because of what comes next.

phrases.english: They have no fixed time.
Would you say the same about the burnt-offering of appearance,
which has a fixed time?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל: מָה לִנְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the קל וחומר from step 4 against בית שמאי's objection in step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נדרים ונדבות show that offerings are not allowed on יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: נדרים ונדבות are different because they have no fixed time. A עולת ראיה does have one.

steps.title: בית שמאי: the burnt-offering of appearance has no fixed day either
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי argue that a עולת ראיה also has no fixed time. They bring a משנה showing it can be brought on any day of the חג.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: This one also has no fixed time. We learned in a משנה: someone who did not bring his offering on the first day of the חג may keep bringing it the whole holiday, even on the last day.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי push back on בית הלל's distinction. They use a משנה to show that the עולת ראיה is not tied to the first day of the holiday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the offering can be brought on any day of the חג, there is no need to bring it on יום טוב itself. It could be brought on חול המועד. So, according to בית שמאי, it is just as flexible as נדרים ונדבות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As we learned' in a משנה
Here, a verb: he brought the holiday offering
The pilgrimage festival, all of its days
The last holy day of the holiday (שמיני עצרת)

phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אַף זוֹ אֵין קָבוּעַ לָהּ זְמַן,
phrases.english: This one too has no fixed time,
as we learned: one who did not bring his holiday offering
on the first holy day of the חג
may keep bringing it through the entire festival,
including the last holy day of the חג.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי: אַף זוֹ אֵין קָבוּעַ לָהּ זְמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the distinction that בית הלל made in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that a עולת ראיה has a fixed time
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The offering may be brought on any day of the חג, so it is not tied to יום טוב.

steps.title: בית הלל: the whole festival is its fixed time
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל answer that the עולת ראיה still has a fixed time: the festival as a whole. Once the festival is over, the obligation ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to them: This one does have a fixed time. We learned in a משנה: if the festival passed and he did not bring it, he is not responsible for it anymore.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל defend their distinction with a different משנה. It shows the offering is limited to the days of the festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The time window is wide, but it does end. נדרים ונדבות can be paid at any time. A עולת ראיה is lost once the רגל is over, so it really is a holiday-bound offering.

keyTerms.meaning: The festival has passed
Responsibility to make it up

steps.confusionAlert: בית הלל are not saying the offering must be brought on one specific day. They mean the whole festival is its set time, and after that the chance is gone.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to them:
This one too has a fixed time.
As we learned: if the festival passed and he did not bring his holiday offering,
he is not responsible to make it up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל: אַף זוֹ קָבוּעַ לָהּ זְמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בית שמאי's objection in step 7 and saves the distinction from step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the offering can be brought on any day of the חג, it has no fixed time.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole festival is its fixed time, because the obligation ends when the festival ends.

steps.title: בית שמאי: the verse says 'for you,' not for the Most High
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי move from logic to a פסוק. Cooking on יום טוב is allowed 'for you', meaning for people and not for offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: Doesn't the verse already say 'for you'? That means for you, and not for the Most High.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי bring a new argument from a פסוק to support their view that offerings are not allowed on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission to prepare food on יום טוב is written as 'for you'. בית שמאי read this word as a limit: only food for people is allowed, not offerings for גבוה. This would block בית הלל's קל וחומר outright.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But wasn't it already said?' Introduces a פסוק as a challenge
'For you', the word in the פסוק about preparing food on יום טוב
'The Most High', meaning offerings to הקב״ה

phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to them:
But wasn't it already stated: "for you"?
That means for you, and not for the Most High.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר: ״לָכֶם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the argument about fixed time and attacks with a פסוק instead.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's permission to bring offerings on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק limits יום טוב preparation to 'for you', which leaves out offerings to גבוה.

steps.title: בית הלל: 'to ה׳' includes offerings, and 'for you' excludes gentiles and dogs
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל answer with another פסוק, 'לה׳', which includes everything for הקב״ה. They then explain that 'לכם' comes to leave out gentiles and dogs.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to them: Doesn't the verse already say 'to ה׳'? Everything that is for ה׳ is allowed. If so, why does the verse say 'for you'? For you and not for gentiles; for you and not for dogs.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל answer the פסוק with a פסוק. Then they give 'לכם' a different job so it no longer hurts their view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לה׳' shows the festival is also for הקב״ה, so offerings are included. That means 'לכם' cannot be excluding offerings. Instead it excludes cooking for gentiles or for dogs.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To ה׳', from the פסוק about keeping the festival
'What does the verse come to teach?'
Gentiles

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל: offerings are allowed on יום טוב because of 'לה׳'. The word 'לכם' only excludes cooking for gentiles and dogs.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to them:
But wasn't it already stated: "to ה׳"?
That means anything that is for ה׳.
If so, why does the verse say "for you"?
For you, and not for gentiles;
for you, and not for dogs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל, וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר: ״לַה׳״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בית שמאי's פסוק from step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-verse plus a new reading of the opposing verse
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לה׳' includes offerings, and 'לכם' excludes gentiles and dogs.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule that one may not cook on יום טוב for gentiles or for animals.

steps.title: אבא שאול's version: your Master's stove should not be closed when yours is open
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול reports בית הלל's argument in a different form, using the picture of 'your stove' and 'your Master's stove', and adds that it is only fair.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says it differently: On a day when your stove is closed (שבת), your Master's stove is open. So on a day when your stove is open (יום טוב), isn't it obvious that your Master's stove is open too? It is also only fair that your table should not be full while your Master's table is empty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another version of בית הלל's argument, said in אבא שאול's words. It is the same קל וחומר, told with a picture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Your stove' stands for cooking for yourself, and 'your Master's stove' is the מזבח. On שבת you may not cook, yet offerings are brought. So on יום טוב, when you may cook, offerings should surely be allowed. He adds a point of fairness: a person should not feast while the מזבח stays empty.

keyTerms.meaning: In a different wording
A stove
Closed / open, meaning not allowed / allowed to cook
A table; 'your Master's table' is the מזבח

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says it in a different wording:
If, where your stove is closed,
phrases.notes: That's שבת, when you can't cook for yourself.

phrases.english: your Master's stove is open,
phrases.notes: Your Master's stove is the מזבח.

phrases.english: then where your stove is open,
isn't it logical that your Master's stove is open?
And it is also only fair
that your table should not be full
while your Master's table is empty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמְרָהּ בְּלָשׁוֹן אַחֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of בית הלל's קל וחומר from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since offerings are brought on שבת when personal cooking is forbidden, they should surely be brought on יום טוב when personal cooking is allowed.

steps.title: What do the two versions disagree about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the real disagreement is between the first ברייתא and אבא שאול's version of בית הלל's argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has two versions of the same debate, and now asks what the actual difference between them is. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just saw אבא שאול report בית הלל's argument differently from the first ברייתא. The גמרא wants to know whether this is only a difference in style or a real difference in הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: He means the first ברייתא and אבא שאול, who told בית הלל's argument in two different ways.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי קָא מִפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what practical difference lies behind the two versions just presented.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The halachic point on which the first ברייתא and אבא שאול differ.

steps.title: The disagreement is about vow and gift offerings on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: One version holds נדרים ונדבות may be brought on יום טוב, and the other holds they may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds that vow offerings and gift offerings may be brought on יום טוב. The other Sage holds that they may not be brought on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two versions disagree about whether voluntary offerings (נדרים ונדבות) may be brought on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first ברייתא, בית שמאי can use נדרים ונדבות as a counter-example only because בית הלל agree those offerings are forbidden on יום טוב. אבא שאול's version has no such exchange, because in his version בית הלל hold that even נדרים ונדבות are brought, as 'your Master's stove' is fully open.

keyTerms.meaning: Vow offerings and gift offerings: voluntary קרבנות a person takes upon himself
Are offered, are brought on the מזבח
One Sage holds

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: נְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת קְרֵבִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One Sage holds: vow offerings and gift offerings may be brought on a Festival,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַר סָבַר: אֵין קְרֵבִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: they may not be brought on a Festival.
phrases.notes: This is the side of the first ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר נְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת קְרֵבִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree whether נדרים ונדבות may be offered on יום טוב.

steps.title: The ban on vow offerings is from the Torah, not a rabbinic decree
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says that according to the view forbidding נדרים ונדבות on יום טוב, the reason is not a rabbinic fear of delay. They are forbidden by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: According to the one who says vow and gift offerings may not be brought on יום טוב, do not say that by Torah law they are fit and the Rabbis forbade them out of fear that a person would delay bringing them. Rather, even by Torah law they are not fit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא clarifies why, according to the stricter view, these offerings may not be brought on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the Torah allows them and the Rabbis forbade them so people would not hold off their offerings until the festival. רב הונא rejects this: the Torah itself does not allow them on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law
A rabbinic protective decree
Lest he delay (bringing his offering)
They are fit

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
According to the one who says that vow and gift offerings
may not be brought on a Festival,
do not say: by Torah law they really are fit,
and it is the Rabbis who made a decree about them,
a decree lest he delay,
phrases.notes: The worry would be that he puts off his offering until the festival, when he is anyway coming to the בית המקדש.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא נָמֵי לָא חָזוּ.
phrases.english: rather, even by Torah law they are not fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא לְדִבְרֵי הָאוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the stricter view mentioned in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the view forbidding נדרים ונדבות on יום טוב, the ban is from the Torah, not a rabbinic גזירה.

steps.title: Proof from the two loaves of שבועות
steps.stepSummary: The שתי הלחם are a required offering of the day, so there is no fear of delay, yet their preparation does not override שבת or יום טוב. This shows a Torah rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the two loaves are an obligation of the day, and there is no reason to fear a person will delay them, yet they do not override שבת or יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא brings a proof that the rule is from the Torah, using the שתי הלחם brought on שבועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'lest he delay' worry cannot apply to the שתי הלחם, since they can only be brought on שבועות. Even so, they are not prepared on שבת or יום טוב. So there must be a Torah rule that only what must be done on the festival itself may be done then, and that same rule keeps out נדרים ונדבות.

keyTerms.meaning: The two loaves of wheat brought on שבועות
An obligation tied to that day
Overrides (a prohibition)

steps.whatToRemember: According to this view, the Torah only lets you do things on יום טוב that belong to that day. A voluntary offering does not, so it is forbidden by Torah law.

phrases.english: For the two loaves,
which are an obligation of the day,
and there is no reason to decree lest he delay,
phrases.notes: They can only be brought on שבועות, so nobody could put them off until then.

phrases.english: yet it does not override Shabbat
nor the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָא שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב הונא's claim in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That the ban on נדרים ונדבות on יום טוב is from the Torah.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The שתי הלחם do not override שבת or יום טוב even though there is no fear of delay.

steps.title: What if someone slaughtered a vow offering on יום טוב anyway?
steps.stepSummary: According to the view forbidding נדרים ונדבות on יום טוב, the גמרא asks what the הלכה is if someone went ahead and slaughtered one.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: according to the one who says vow and gift offerings may not be brought on יום טוב, if someone broke the rule and slaughtered one, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question: after the forbidden slaughter has already happened, what may be done next? This sets up two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slaughter is done, but the blood still needs to be sprinkled on the מזבח. The question is whether that next step is allowed on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them
He broke the rule and slaughtered

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
According to the one who says that vow and gift offerings
may not be brought on a Festival,
if he transgressed and slaughtered, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ לְדִבְרֵי הָאוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the stricter view and asks about a case where the rule was already broken.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the blood may be sprinkled after a forbidden slaughter on יום טוב.

steps.title: רבא: sprinkle the blood so the meat may be eaten
steps.stepSummary: רבא says he sprinkles the blood in order to permit the meat to be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: He sprinkles the blood in order to permit the meat to be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers that the blood may be sprinkled, because doing so allows people to eat the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until the blood is sprinkled, the meat may not be eaten. Since eating is a need of people on יום טוב, רבא allows the sprinkling for that purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: He sprinkles the blood on the מזבח
For the purpose of

phrases.english: Rava said:
He sprinkles the blood
in order to permit the meat to be eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר זוֹרֵק אֶת הַדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The blood is sprinkled so that the meat becomes permitted to eat.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא: sprinkle the blood to burn the fats at night
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא says he sprinkles the blood in order to burn the אימורין in the evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: He sprinkles the blood in order to burn the sacrificial parts in the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב הונא agrees the blood is sprinkled but gives a different purpose: burning the אימורין in the evening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אמוראים let the blood be sprinkled, but they explain its purpose differently. רבא connects it to eating the meat, while רבה בר רב הונא connects it to burning the fats on the מזבח in the evening.

keyTerms.meaning: The fats and parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח
To burn (on the מזבח)
In the evening

steps.whatToRemember: Both אמוראים allow sprinkling the blood after a forbidden slaughter, but רבא ties it to eating the meat and רבה בר רב הונא ties it to burning the אימורין in the evening.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
He sprinkles the blood
in order to burn the sacrificial parts in the evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר זוֹרֵק אֶת הַדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 16, with a different purpose for the sprinkling than רבא's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The blood is sprinkled so that the אימורין can be burned in the evening.

steps.title: What is the difference between רבא and רבה בר רב הונא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two reasons for sprinkling the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that רבא and רבה בר רב הונא both say to sprinkle the blood. It asks when their different reasons would actually lead to a different ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says the blood is sprinkled so the meat can be eaten. רבה בר רב הונא says it is sprinkled so the אימורין can be burned at night. Since both reach the same result in a normal case, the גמרא looks for a case where they split.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? It asks for the practical difference between two opinions.
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח.
The fats and parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: "Them" means רבא and רבה בר רב הונא from the last two steps.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical difference between the two answers given in steps 17 and 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two reasons for sprinkling the blood lead to different rulings.

steps.title: The difference: when the meat became impure or was lost
steps.stepSummary: If the meat became טמא or was lost, רבא says not to sprinkle, but רבה בר רב הונא says to sprinkle.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them when the meat became impure or was lost. According to רבא, he does not sprinkle. According to רבה בר רב הונא, he does sprinkle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a case where the two reasons split: the meat can no longer be eaten because it became טמא or was lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the only reason to sprinkle on יום טוב is to let the meat be eaten. If the meat is gone or טמא, there is no reason left, so he does not sprinkle. For רבה בר רב הונא, the reason is to burn the אימורין at night, and that still applies, so he sprinkles.

keyTerms.meaning: Became ritually impure (טמא).
Was lost.
He sprinkles (the blood).
He does not sprinkle.

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: no edible meat means no sprinkling. רבה בר רב הונא: sprinkle anyway, for the sake of the אימורין.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
when the meat became impure or was lost.
According to רבא, he does not sprinkle,
according to רבה בר רב הונא, he does sprinkle.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ נִטְמָא בָּשָׂר אוֹ שֶׁאָבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the meat is טמא or lost, רבא does not sprinkle and רבה בר רב הונא does.

steps.title: A ברייתא about the שבועות lambs: do not sprinkle on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a challenge from a ברייתא. Lambs of שבועות slaughtered for the wrong purpose or at the wrong time have their blood sprinkled, but not on שבת. The ruling for someone who sprinkled anyway continues in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: The lambs of שבועות that were slaughtered not for their own purpose, or slaughtered either before their time or after their time, have their blood sprinkled and their meat eaten. If it was שבת, he should not sprinkle. And if he did sprinkle...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא to challenge the view just discussed. The quote is not finished here, so this step sets up a point that will become clear in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a weekday, these lambs are still valid קרבנות, so the blood is sprinkled and the meat is eaten. On שבת, the ברייתא says not to sprinkle, even though sprinkling would also allow the אימורין to be burned. That seems to clash with רבה בר רב הונא, who sprinkles for the sake of the אימורין. The ending, "and if he sprinkled," sets up the rest of the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection. It introduces a challenge from a תנאי source.
The two lambs brought as שלמים with the שתי הלחם on שבועות.
Not for their own purpose, meaning slaughtered with the intent of a different קרבן.
Before their time or after their time, meaning not on the proper day.
It (the blood) shall be sprinkled.

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is cut off at "and if he sprinkled." Don't decide yet how the challenge works. Its full point comes in the next lines.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
The lambs of שבועות that one slaughtered not for their own purpose,
or that he slaughtered either before their time
or after their time,
the blood is sprinkled and the meat is eaten.
And if it was שבת, he should not sprinkle.
And if he did sprinkle...

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the difference is defined in step 20, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that appears to challenge רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר רב הונא's view that the blood is sprinkled for the sake of burning the אימורין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids sprinkling on שבת even though the אימורין could be burned afterward. That suggests burning the אימורין is not enough reason to sprinkle. The full force of the challenge depends on the ending, which comes next.
